Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority,

to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 9796 - 1981 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
NON-WEATHERTIGHT STEEL DOORS 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 27 February 1981, after the draft finalized by the Shipbuilding 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo 
Movement and Packaging Division Council ( MCPDC ■). 

0.2 While using this standard, reference to the following Indian Standards 
is considered essential: 

18:8712-1978 Guidelines for co-ordination of dimensions in 
shipbuilding 

Part I Principles of dimensional co-ordination 

Part II Glossary of terms 

Part III Co-ordination sizes for components and assemblies 

Part IV Controlling dimensions 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the general requirements and basic dimensions 
of non-weathertight steel doors. 

1.2 This standard does not cover special size doors. 

2. TYPES 

2.1 The non-weathertight steel doors shall be classified as follows: 

a) Type A and B — The maximum door width shall be 700 mm; 

b) Type C and D — The maximum door width shall be 800 mm; and 

c) Type E and F — The maximum door width shall be 1200 mm. 
The door panel shall be in the two parts.

4.1 The main dimensions of non-weathertight steel doors shall be as 
given in Table 2.

4.2 The principal dimensions of non-weathertight steel doors shall be as 
shown in Fig. 1 and 2. 

4.3 The dimensions of hinge shall be as shown in Fig 3. 

4.4 The dimensions of handle shall be as shown in Fig 4. 

4.5 The dimensions in closed position shall be as shown in Fig 5 and 6. 

4.6 The dimensions of hook shall be as shown in Fig. 7. 

4.7 The dimensions of hook used for locking the door in open position 
shall be as shown in Fig. 8 and 9. 

4.8 The dimensions of locking arrangement of door shall be as shown in 
Fig. 10. 

5. TOLERANCES 

5.1 The allowable tolerances on all dimensions shall be of coarse series 
according to IS : 2102-1969*. 

6. CONSTRUCTION 

6.1 The doors shall be fitted in such a way that when in closed position 
the gaps between the edge of door panel and cut in steel bulkhead shall 
not exceed 5 mm in any case. 

6.2 Each door or door panel shall be fitted with two hinges in the position 
shown in Fig. 1 and 2. 

6.3 Handles and locking arrangement shall be so fitted as not to be at a 
height greater than 1 000 mm from deck. Door handles shall be fitted 
on both sides. 

6.4 The door panels shall be stiffened suitably either by the method of 
swedging or by welded stiffeners. 

7. DESIGNATION 

7.1 The door shall be designated by its name, type and direction of 
opening — right hand opening ( R ) and left hand opening ( L ). 

Example: 

A non-weathertight door of Type A with a right hand opening 
shall be designated as: 

Non-weathertight door, Type A, ( R ). 



'Specification for allowable deviations for dimensions without specified tolerances 

(first revision ). 



IS : 9796 - 1981 
8. MARKING 

8.1 The doors may be marked with the ISI Certification Mark. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of 
the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks )Act and the Rules and Regula- 
tions made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the require- 
ments of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. 
ISI marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for 
the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, 
may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution,
